decisions.question: In general form, how is a contract with more than one producing leaf-parent replayed under item 10, given that 'unrestricted at the last phase that produces the contract' has no single reading for two producers?

options.label: per-producer shares, each case within exactly one share
options.consequence: Each producer's phases restrict file and cli to what that producer has delivered; its last producing phase runs restricted to its whole share; the last replays together run every case; --all at nidana.integration is the one unrestricted replay. Adds a condition (every case falls within exactly one share) that the replay tool cannot check, so it is checked by reading.

options.label: per-producer shares, no coverage condition
options.consequence: Same replays, but a case whose ids span two shares or fall within none would run at no producing gate and first meet a real producer at nidana.integration's --all, silently.

options.label: literal reading: the last-merging producer replays unrestricted
options.consequence: The producer whose last phase merges second runs the other producer's cases, so it needs an ordering edge no contract carries, and which producer carries it depends on merge order.

decisions.chosen: per-producer shares, each case within exactly one share
decisions.why: It is nidana.tooling D2's reading, which the step asked to write in general form, plus the one condition that makes D2's conclusion 'together, every case the contract has' hold for any such contract rather than by coincidence. 'Falls within' reuses item 9's rule (a case runs only when every id it covers is in the restriction), so no new mechanism is introduced. The condition is needed because shares may overlap on an id each host meets on its own (G3 in nidana-checks@v1): a case covering only a shared id would run at both producers' gates and fail at the one that lacks the host. nidana-checks@v1 meets it as written: an inline check of its seventeen Covers cells against lint's G1 to G8 and codegen's G3 and G9 to G18 put each case within exactly one share (analyze-* in lint's, scan-* in codegen's). Restriction covers file and cli only, because behavior belongs to api and shared-model contracts (item 4), which decision 2 keeps single-producer.

decisions.question: The general form must also say what happens to the sets item 10 runs in full (surface, reject) when a contract has several producers: item 10 justifies running them in full by 'the first phase of the producing leaf-parent lands every declaration', which assumes one producer.

options.label: api and shared-model contracts have one producing leaf-parent
options.consequence: States the presumption item 10 already relies on; every api and shared-model contract in the tree already has one leaf-parent producer, so nothing changes now; a future decomposition that splits one must change item 10 first.

options.label: leave the full-run sets' consequence unstated
options.consequence: Literal text stays as is, but a second producer's first gate would run surface and reject over declarations its own first phase cannot land (ADR-002 item 3 gives each package one owner), and fail; the trap is found only when a decomposition hits it.

options.label: allow several producers, each replaying its own declarations
options.consequence: Needs a producer mark on each surface and reject library and a new restriction mechanism, since --guarantee restricts neither set.

decisions.chosen: api and shared-model contracts have one producing leaf-parent
decisions.why: A general rule for multi-producer contracts that is silent on the full-run sets would be wrong for exactly the kinds that have them. nidana.runtime D1 point 1 already used item 10's full surface and reject runs as the reason to keep one leaf-parent producing bus-api@v1 and bus-testing@v1, so the constraint states what the tree already follows. Checked: the nine contracts' kind and produced_by; all seven api or shared-model contracts have one leaf-parent producer. This goes beyond the step's text, which named the restricted replay only, so it is marked would_have_asked. It is not a run-stop: no current node or contract differs between the options. Signal that would have changed it: a planned decomposition that wants to split an api contract between packages, which would favor the third option and its tool work.

decisions.question: Where are the producers' shares of a multi-producer contract recorded?

options.label: the spec of the node whose decomposition made the producers
options.consequence: Matches where nidana.tooling D2 already put them; the contract text stays free of tree facts; the replay tool and structure cannot check the share condition, so hsdd-contract and hsdd-phase-plan check it by reading.

options.label: the contract's ## Validation
options.consequence: structure could check each case falls within exactly one share, but every decomposition would need a contract touch to write the shares, and the contract is written before its producers exist.

decisions.chosen: the spec of the node whose decomposition made the producers
decisions.why: nidana-checks@v1's Boundary leaves the division of its hosts to nidana.tooling's decomposition, and D2 already holds the shares; moving them would cost a contract touch for a check that today has one contract and seventeen cases to read. Close call; the signal that would have changed it: a multi-producer contract whose cases change often, where a case spanning two shares could slip past reading.

decisions.question: Do nidana.tooling.codegen and nidana.tooling.lint belong in ADR-001's affects, and does nidana.tooling stay?

options.label: add both children, keep nidana.tooling
options.consequence: affects matches every spec that says Governed by ADR-001; no node spec changes.

options.label: add both children, drop nidana.tooling
options.consequence: nidana.tooling's spec would still say Governed by ADR-001 with no matching affects entry, which the linking rule forbids, and its D2 reads item 10.

options.label: leave affects unchanged
options.consequence: gate.mjs passes, but both children say Governed by ADR-001 and produce the contracts item 10 governs, so the two sides disagree.

decisions.why: Both child specs (and nidana.tooling's embedded child blocks) already carry Governed by: [ADR-001, ADR-002], and both produce contracts whose gates item 10 sets, so they are affected. nidana.tooling remains an internal node whose spec carries the link. No Governed by line needed editing; nidana.runtime has no children and is unchanged.
